title: spec authoring-port/v1
description: Versioned contract for the MCP tools an agent session uses to author specs through spec's own engines. Tools are tiered by authority: the authoring tier is available in any agent session, while the transition tier is opt-in via preferences.agent_authoring.transitions and is absent from tools/list when disabled. Evolution is additive-only within this major version: new optional fields and new tools may appear, existing field meanings and required sets may not change. Unknown optional fields are tolerated by both sides.

authoring.description: Always available in an agent session. Every write is recoverable from the specs-repo diff, which is what makes on-by-default defensible.

transition.description: Opt-in. Stage transitions fire the pipeline's configured effects (PM status sync, comms posts) exactly as the CLI does, so an agent moving a spec would notify a team on the user's behalf. Gating the tool answers the authority question without weakening the transition.

toolResult.description: Every tool returns success plus a human- and model-readable message. Expected negative outcomes (a stale hash, an unmet gate, a disabled tier) are reported as success:false with a message naming the next action, not as protocol errors.

contentHash.description: SHA-256 of a section body after canonical formatting, prefixed with its algorithm. Hashing the formatted body rather than submitted bytes is load-bearing: a write reformats what it is given, so hashing the input would make the hash a writer receives disagree with the hash a later reader computes, and every second write in a session would raise a spurious conflict.

spec_section_read.description: Read one section's body plus its content_hash.
spec_section_read.returns: content_hash line followed by the section body

spec_section_write.description: Replace a section body through the markdown engine: validated, formatted, and logged with agent attribution.

content.description: Section body in markdown, without the heading

base_hash.description: content_hash from spec_section_read. When present and stale, the call fails with a structured conflict and the file is left byte-identical. When absent, the write is unchecked — intended for callers where a human is the lock, not for agent sessions.

spec_section_write.returns: the new content_hash, so consecutive writes need no intervening read
errors: CONFLICT: the section changed since base_hash was read

spec_acceptance_add.description: Append one acceptance criterion to §6. Idempotent: an identical criterion already present is a no-op success, compared ignoring checkbox state so a criterion the user has already ticked is not duplicated.

criterion.description: A single testable criterion, without the checkbox prefix

spec_meta_update.description: Update a fixed set of frontmatter fields. The allowed set is an explicit list rather than a passthrough map, so a frontmatter field added later is not silently writable by an agent the day it appears.
errors: stage/status cannot be set here — use the transition tools, which run the gates

spec_advance.description: Advance a spec to the next stage. Runs the same gates as the CLI and fires the pipeline's configured transition effects.
errors: GATE NOT MET: <gate> (<reason>) — the stage is unchanged
stage transitions are disabled for agent sessions — set preferences.agent_authoring.transitions

spec_revert.description: Revert a spec to an earlier stage with a reason.
